sections.title: Preparations at Sinai
sections.description: Census, the camp is organized, service of the Levites

sections.title: The Wilderness Journey
sections.description: From Sinai to the Plains of Moab with rebellion and punishment

sections.title: Balaam
sections.description: Balak and Balaam, blessing instead of curse

sections.title: The Plains of Moab
sections.description: Second census and preparations for entry

events.title: The First Census
events.description: The Lord commands Moses to count all men in Israel fit for war from twenty years old and upward. The census shows 603,550 men, not including the Levites.

events.title: The camp is organized
events.description: God gives instructions about the camp arrangement. The twelve tribes are placed in a specific order around the tabernacle, three tribes on each side, with their banners.

events.title: The Service of the Levites
events.description: The Levites are appointed to serve at the tabernacle in place of the firstborn of Israel. The three Levitical clans, Gershon, Kohath, and Merari, each receive their own tasks for carrying and caring for the sanctuary.

events.title: The Nazirite Vow and the Aaronic Blessing
events.description: God gives the rules for the Nazirite vow and the Aaronic blessing: The Lord bless you and keep you. The Lord make his face shine on you and be gracious to you.

events.title: Departure from Sinai
events.description: In the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day, the cloud lifts from the tabernacle. Israel breaks camp from the wilderness of Sinai and journeys toward the wilderness of Paran in organized order.

events.title: The People's Complaint at Taberah
events.description: The people complain about their hardships, and the Lord's fire burns at the edge of the camp. Moses prays to the Lord, and the fire dies out. The place is called Taberah.

events.title: Quail and God's Wrath
events.description: The people weep for meat and long to return to Egypt. God sends quail in enormous quantities but strikes the people with a severe plague while the meat is still between their teeth. The place is called Kibroth-hattaavah.

events.title: Miriam and Aaron Oppose Moses
events.description: Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses because of his Cushite wife and challenge his unique position. God speaks directly to them and strikes Miriam with leprosy. After Moses' intercession, she is healed after seven days of being outside the camp.

events.title: The Twelve Spies
events.description: Moses sends twelve spies into Canaan. After 40 days they return. Ten spies give a negative report and say the people in the land are too strong. Only Caleb and Joshua encourage them to go in.

events.title: God's Judgment: 40 Years in the Wilderness
events.description: The people rebel and want to choose a new leader to return to Egypt. God judges the entire generation to wander in the wilderness for 40 years. No one over twenty years old will see the promised land, except Caleb and Joshua.

events.title: Korah's Rebellion
events.description: Korah, Dathan and Abiram rebel against Moses and Aaron and challenge their leadership. The earth opens up and swallows the rebels, and fire from the Lord consumes the 250 men who offered incense.

events.title: Aaron's Staff Budds
events.description: To confirm Aaron's selection, Moses places twelve staffs in the tabernacle, one for each tribe. The next morning, Aaron's staff has budded, blossomed and borne ripe almonds, as a sign from God of his calling.

events.title: Water from the Rock and Moses' Sin
events.description: At Kadesh the people complain about lack of water. God commands Moses to speak to the rock, but Moses strikes it twice with his staff in anger. Water flows out, but God says that Moses and Aaron will not lead the people into the promised land because they did not honor him as holy.

events.title: The Bronze Serpent
events.description: The people complain against God and Moses, and the Lord sends poisonous snakes among them. Many die. Moses makes a bronze snake and sets it on a pole. All who look at it after being bitten will live.

events.title: Balaam's Donkey and Blessings
events.description: King Balak of Moab hires the prophet Balaam to curse Israel. Balaam's donkey sees the angel of the Lord and stops three times. God opens the donkey's mouth. Finally, Balaam blesses Israel four times instead of cursing them, including the prophecy about the star from Jacob.

events.title: The Sin at Baal-Peor
events.description: Israelite men begin to commit sexual immorality with Moabite women and worship their gods at Baal-Peor. God's anger burns, and 24,000 die in a plague. The priest Phinehas stops the plague by killing an Israelite man and a Midianite woman.

events.title: The Second Census
events.description: After the plague, God orders a new census. The new generation counts 601,730 men fit for war. From the first generation, only Caleb and Joshua remain.

events.title: Joshua Appointed as Moses' Successor
events.description: God tells Moses to go up to Mount Abarim and see the land, but not enter it. Moses asks God to appoint a new leader. God chooses Joshua, a man filled with the Spirit, and Moses lays his hands on him before the whole assembly.

events.title: War Against Midian
events.description: The Lord commands Moses to take vengeance on the Midianites for what happened at Baal-Peor. Israel sends 12,000 soldiers who defeat Midian. Balaam is killed in the war.

events.title: The Tribes' Inheritance East of the Jordan
events.description: Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh ask to settle east of the Jordan, where there is good grazing land. Moses agrees on the condition that they first help the other tribes conquer Canaan.
